🚨 RAILWAY CONFIRMS SECURITY INCIDENT: CUSTOMER ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES MAY HAVE BEEN ACCESSED  Cloud deployment platform Railway says it detected anomalous activity on October 21 in systems that store customer environment variables.  According to Railway's security disclosure, an unauthorized third party may have accessed ENCRYPTED environment variables and, for some of them, obtained the DECRYPTED contents.  Those variables can hold:  * API keys * Database credentials * Private registry credentials  Railway's response so far:  * ALL builds and deployments are paused, including for Enterprise customers * All storage bucket credentials are being rotated * Upstream AI inference providers were notified to proactively revoke keys * Affected customers will be contacted directly by email  Railway believes the incident is part of a series of attacks targeting platform companies with the aim of compromising AI inference providers.  Initial analysis suggests a subset of users may be affected, but Railway recommends ALL users act now.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If you run anything on Railway, rotate every secret stored there (API keys, database and registry credentials) and review service logs for unusual activity. Because deployments are paused, new credentials cannot be rolled out until builds resume, so revoke keys at the provider side where you can. The AI-provider angle matters: stolen inference API keys are routinely resold or abused for compute.  blog.railway.com/p/security-… #Railway #DataBreach #CloudSecurity #APIKeys #SupplyChainSecurity #AISecurity #ThreatIntel #DDW

Public PoC claims ASLR-bypass RCE on unpatched PHP  A public proof-of-concept exploit has been released on GitHub targeting the PHP session flaws behind "PHP2Shell". The author says it achieves one-shot, fully remote code execution on an unpatched PHP 8.4.26 + Apache stack (mod_php, prefork), bypassing ASLR over plain HTTP with no code added to the target page.  * The PoC runs against the official php:8.4.26-apache image; the author reports a 3/3 success rate yielding www-data command execution. * It leaks heap and PHP library addresses to defeat ASLR; the current version needs display_errors=on. * This targets unpatched 8.4.26 - fixed builds already exist.  Patch now: update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, or your vendor's fixed package.  github.com/9bie/php2shell-by… #PHP #CyberSecurity

sample_tweets.text: Since my posts have been shared here ~30 times in the past few weeks, it seems like I'm going to be contributing to Space Karen's Ketamine Extravaganza whether I like it or not.  I don't really intend to be active here, but I'll post some of the more important cybersecurity-focused stuff, since it gets screenshotted anyway. That way, people don't have to read post a week late and out of context.

Current information I have on php2Shell:  - The RCEs requires the attacker to obtain memory addresses which are typically protected by ASLR.  - I suspect the original author (lcfr_hax) likely has a reliable exploit which leads to stable code execution.  - Most of the PoCs being posted are completely non-functional AI slop.  - There is at least 1 working non-slop exploit being passed around, but it's reliant on bruteforcing for ASLR bypass, so not particularly impactful.  - Rumor of ITW exploitation are patchy. There are attempts being seen using the non-functional leaked RCE, or variants that are config / system specific.  - Some rumors point towards a known-working exploit being used by threat actors (I've personally confirmed this specific exploit works, but the ASLR bypass technique is unreliable at best and massively limits the potential impact).  - I'd expect heavy ITW exploitation in the next few weeks based on how many people are looking at this. Though, success rates will vary heavily based on the specific exploit chain.

🚨🇫🇷 GlassWorm-linked actors hijacked OVHcloud CLI releases to spread credential-stealing malware A compromised developer GitHub account was used to replace binaries attached to OVHcloud CLI releases v0.11.0 through v0.15.0 on October 19. ⠀ The malicious downloads were available between 12:47 and 14:21 UTC and were downloaded approximately 250 times. Only users who installed or updated the CLI during that window are affected. Earlier downloads of those versions remain safe. ⠀ The malware targeted data belonging to VS Code, Cursor, Claude, OpenCode and other developer tools, alongside AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Docker, Kubernetes, npm, DigitalOcean, SSH and Terraform credentials. ⠀ OVHcloud traced the compromise to GitHub credentials stolen after a developer installed a malicious VS Code extension on a personal MacBook in October 2025. Infrastructure linked to the incident contained indicators previously associated with GlassWorm. ⠀ OVHcloud says its source code and build systems were not compromised and no other repositories were affected. The malicious files were removed, release immutability was enabled and version 0.16.0 was published as a clean release. Anyone who ran an affected binary should treat secrets stored on that system as compromised, revoke or rotate them, remove the binary and install version 0.16.0.

🚨 LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromised to steal cloud, developer and AI credentials LiteLLM, an open-source gateway used to connect applications with multiple AI providers, was compromised through a malicious release published on PyPI and official container registries. ⠀ All seven LiteLLM 1.107.0 wheels were affected across Windows, macOS and Linux. The malware uses Python startup files to execute whenever Python launches, even if LiteLLM is never imported. ⠀ Researchers found it targeting: • AWS, Azure and Google Cloud credentials • Kubernetes, Vault and Terraform secrets • SSH, GPG and TLS private keys • Git tokens, .env files and browser data • Credentials for Codex, Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf and Hugging Face ⠀ A separate loader was designed to check attacker-controlled infrastructure every hour and execute additional Python code. PyPI and Docker Hub have removed the malicious release and affected images. Anyone who installed LiteLLM 1.107.0 or pulled the latest, main-latest or main-stable container tags while they pointed to it should isolate affected systems, rotate accessible credentials from a clean device and rebuild from a trusted release.

🚨🇮🇳 State Bank of India investigates dark web exposure of customer records State Bank of India, the country’s largest lender, says it identified 3,897 customer records containing personal information while examining approximately 375,000 records found on the dark web. ⠀ The exposed information reportedly includes names, gender, mobile numbers, dates of birth, email and residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs and metadata linked to loan records. ⠀ SBI was alerted on October 16 by its threat intelligence provider, India’s Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In. The bank activated its incident response procedures and hired an independent cybersecurity firm to investigate the source and extent of the exposure. ⠀ SBI says its core operations remain unaffected and customer balances are safe. The authenticity and completeness of the exposed data are still being assessed. Source: https://www. ndtv.com/business-news/sbi-dat a-leak-cyberattack-customer-account-phone-records-hacker-dark-web-12213824
